item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may change these edits at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

Heh. Honestly, the part I find the most endearing about this article is the application of computer problems to the real world to dramatic effect. Its both hilarious and terrifying at the same time. In that vein of thinking, both collaborative tales Technical Issues and New Technical Issues often feature 713 and would make solid crosslinks. Considering how those tales link to other technology based skips, such a link here would really go the extra mile in opening up the wikiwalk. As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Change this:

Every effort must be made to avoid crashing SCP-713. When the machine locks up, its cursor either disappears immediately, dropping any held object, or [DATA EXPUNGED] consistent with crushing forces of over ████ kN. Other error types have commensurately more damaging results. See experiment logs and incident reports for further details.

To this:

Every effort must be made to avoid crashing SCP-713. When the machine locks up, its cursor either disappears immediately, dropping any held object, or [DATA EXPUNGED] consistent with crushing forces of over ████ kN. Other error types have commensurately more damaging results. See experiment logs and incident reports for further details.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Much as I like it, some issues I have:

1. If you can just lock it in a box somewhere, not mess with it, and have nothing happen, then it should be Safe, not Euclid. Euclid means that if you lock something in a box and leave it alone, then there's no telling what will happen.

2. As it is, it seems too predictable and tidy. You perform a function, it does exactly as programmed every time. That's… not realistic for any Win95 system, much less one modified to SCP specifications. I'd expect more blue screens and general protection faults and illegal operations, with all the attendant consequences. (It would also make it more dangerous to use and could possibly earn it its Euclid class.)

3. The picture has speakers, which contradicts the description of having only mouse, keyboard, and monitor. There's also no mention of CD-Rom or floppy drives, but that's a minor point.

('Course, since it's about to hit double digits, the feedback may be moot anyway.)
